transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, what brought me in is... I've been noticing that I just keep getting up when I'm supposed to be sitting down. Like in our department meetings at the high school, or even just at dinner at home. Everyone else is seated, and I'll suddenly just feel this need to go refill my coffee or check a handout. 

Which reminds me, the main copier in the faculty lounge has been jammed for going on three weeks now, and it's just a nightmare because I teach tenth-grade history and I really rely on printing out primary sources for the kids. The principal keeps saying they're getting a new one, but you know how the district budget is right now. My husband told me I should just use the one at the public library, but the parking there is absolutely terrible since they started that water main construction on Elm Street. It took me twenty minutes just to find a spot last Tuesday... 

Oh, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Right, the sitting. But yeah, I just end up walking to the back of the room or getting up from the table even though nothing is actually urgent. I just can't seem to stay in my seat like everyone else.

Can you tell me whether you've experienced this kind of restlessness and difficulty staying seated for as long as you can remember, even back in childhood or school, or is this something that's started more recently?

Oh, no, it's definitely not recent. It's been forever. Even as a little girl, my report cards always said the exact same thing—that I was a bright student, but I just could not stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother actually used to joke that I wore a permanent path into the floorboards between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was even ten years old! 

Speaking of pencil sharpeners, do you remember those heavy metal crank ones they used to screw right into the wall? We had one in my classroom that finally broke last year, and getting maintenance to replace it was an absolute saga. They ended up giving us these cheap little electric ones that just chew up the colored pencils, which is so frustrating. The kids really need their colored pencils for their map assignments. We're doing the Silk Road unit right now, which is just fascinating, honestly. I love teaching it because Marco Polo is such an interesting historical figure, and the way the trade routes connected... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I did it again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, childhood. But yes, to answer your question, I've always been this way, ever since I was a little girl.

Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, lose track of what you're doing, or forget important details—like you did a couple of times just now while we were talking?

Focus? No, I wouldn't say that at all. I'm actually very sharp with details, especially when I'm working. My lesson plans are meticulously organized, and I never forget a deadline or lose track of my grading. I keep everything in these beautiful leather-bound planners. 

My daughter actually got me a customized one for my sixtieth birthday last month. We went up to Chicago for the weekend to celebrate, just the two of us, and had the most wonderful time. We went to this Italian place off the Magnificent Mile, and the pasta was just... well, they make it from scratch right there in the window. You can stand on the sidewalk and watch them kneading the dough. It reminds me of when my grandmother used to make pierogis in her tiny kitchen when I was little. She had this old wooden rolling pin that weighed an absolute ton, and she would let me help her pinch the edges of the dough together... 

Oh, but what were we saying? Right, my focus. No, I don't really have trouble focusing on my actual tasks or forgetting important things. I just get carried away when I'm chatting, I suppose!
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, finishing other people's sentences, or blurting out responses before someone has finished speaking?

Well, yes, actually. I do that quite a bit. Especially in group discussions, like at our curriculum meetings or my monthly book club. Someone will be talking, and I already have the response in my head, and I just... blurt it out before they've even finished their thought. I just can't seem to stop myself! 

Speaking of book club, we're reading this historical fiction novel right now about the wives of Henry VIII, and it is just phenomenal. We usually meet at Sarah's house—she's the AP English teacher—and she always makes these incredible charcuterie boards. Last time she had this aged gouda that was just to die for. She gets it from this little artisanal cheese shop downtown, the one right next to the old movie theater that they just renovated. They're showing classic films there now, which is so wonderful because I've always loved Audrey Hepburn. *Roman Holiday* is an absolute masterpiece, don't you think? The way they captured the city of Rome... 

Oh, gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I completely lost my train of thought. What were we talking about? Oh, right, interrupting. But yes, I definitely tend to jump in before people are done speaking.

Have there been specific periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had a lot more energy than is typical for you?

Unusually elated? Like... manic, you mean? No, I wouldn't say I've ever had anything like that. I mean, I have my moments where I'm in a really good mood, especially when the weather turns nice in the spring. Oh, spring is just glorious around here, isn't it? The dogwoods in my front yard bloom this incredible shade of pink. 

My husband and I planted those trees when we first moved into the house thirty years ago. Can you believe it's been thirty years? Time just flies. We had this awful clay soil back then, and we had to bring in bags and bags of topsoil just to get anything to grow. We bought it from this lovely local nursery that used to be out on Highway 9, but they sold the land a few years ago to developers. Now it's just another strip mall with a chain coffee shop. It's such a shame how much the town has changed. We used to know all our neighbors, and now it feels like people just pull into their garages and never come out...

Wait, I'm sorry, I'm rambling again. You were asking about my energy levels? No, I don't have periods where I don't need sleep or feel... euphoric. I just have my regular, everyday energy, which is usually plenty to keep me going!
Would you say that these patterns of restlessness and impulsivity have caused noticeable problems or distress in your work, relationships, or daily life?

Well, yes, I suppose it has. It’s actually started to affect my relationships, both at school and in my community. People just... lose patience with me. Like in our department meetings, Mr. Henderson—he teaches European History—he’ll give me this heavy sigh and stare at me over his glasses when I interrupt. He’s retiring at the end of the year, actually. He and his wife just bought one of those massive RVs, the ones that look like a luxury tour bus? They’re planning to drive down to Florida and just live in it for the entire winter. I cannot fathom living in a space that small with my husband, much less in Florida! The humidity down there just absolutely ruins my hair. We went to Orlando back in the nineties when the kids were little, and I swear I looked like a poodle the entire trip. We did take them to see the manatees, though, which are just the gentlest, sweetest creatures... 

Oh, goodness, I'm so sorry. I'm doing it again. You asked if it causes distress. Yes, it really does. Because people get frustrated with me in those meetings, and at book club too, when I can't sit still or keep blurting things out. I go to these gatherings wanting to socialize and engage with everyone, but I just end up leaving feeling embarrassed instead of connected. It's... well, it's quite disheartening, honestly.

When you're grading papers or reading through lesson materials, do you often find your attention drifting to unrelated things, or do you frequently make careless mistakes because you lost focus partway through the task?

Grading papers? No, I wouldn't say I lose focus or make careless mistakes with that. I've been doing it for so long, it's practically second nature! Though I will say, the papers the students turn in these days... the grammar is just atrocious. Half of them write like they're sending a text message on their phones. We had to confiscate three phones just last week during a midterm. 

The principal, Mr. Davis, has this strict new zero-tolerance policy for them, which I suppose is good, but he's so rigid about it. He used to be in the military, you know. Navy, I think? Or maybe Coast Guard. He has this anchor tattoo on his forearm that you can only see when he rolls his sleeves up in the spring. Spring is when we do the state testing, which is a whole other nightmare. The state mandates these new computerized tests now, and our Wi-Fi in the history wing is just abysmal. The IT guy, Kevin—bless his heart, he really tries—he was crawling around in the ceiling tiles trying to fix the router last month, and he ended up completely covered in dust. He looked exactly like a powdered doughnut! We had to get the janitor to vacuum his jacket...

Oh, dear, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry, my mind just goes a mile a minute. What were you asking? Oh, right, making mistakes when I'm reading lesson materials or grading. No, I don't really have a problem with my attention drifting like that. I just power right through them!
Do you often lose or misplace things you need for daily tasks, like your keys, glasses, or paperwork, or forget to complete routine errands and chores?

Lose my things? Oh, no, I don't really have a problem with that. Everything has its place in my house. My reading glasses, for instance, are always right on the chain around my neck or on my nightstand. Though I did just get this new pair! I went to Dr. Lin over on Elm Street. He has the loveliest office, they just redecorated the waiting room with these beautiful watercolor landscapes. 

His wife actually paints them! She used to be an art teacher in our district before they had twins. Goodness, twins... I cannot imagine having two babies at once. My sister had twins, boys, and they were just absolute terrors when they were toddlers. They once got into her pantry and poured a five-pound bag of flour all over the kitchen floor. It looked like it had snowed indoors! My sister was furious, of course, and it took her days to get the flour out of the tile grout. They're both in college now, studying engineering, if you can believe it. The one who started the flour incident is actually designing bridges up in Chicago now. It gets so terribly cold in Chicago, I don't know how anyone stands the wind off that lake... 

Oh, for heaven's sake, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just go right off the rails. I am so sorry. You were asking about losing things or forgetting my errands. No, I really don't do that. I've always kept my belongings and my schedule very organized!

{"intent": "Assess whether her tangential thinking reflects a genuine inattention symptom (easily distracted by unrelated thoughts/stimuli during sustained tasks) rather than just talkativeness, which is key to differentiating full combined ADHD criteria from a hyperactive-predominant/unspecified presentation.", "question": "When you're doing something that requires sustained attention, like reading a novel, watching a full movie, or listening to a long lecture or sermon, do you

Well, I suppose it depends on what it is! If I'm reading a novel, I usually power right through it. I actually just finished this wonderful historical fiction book about the court of Henry the Eighth. Goodness, the drama in that court! It's a wonder anyone survived with their head still attached. The author did such a marvelous job describing the clothing, too. All those heavy velvets and the intricate embroidery. It makes me think of my grandmother, actually. She was a seamstress, and she could embroider the most delicate little roses you've ever seen. She made my wedding dress, you know. It was ivory silk with seed pearls all along the bodice. We had the reception at this lovely little country club that had a duck pond out back. My uncle Richard got a little too much champagne in him and actually fell right into the pond! Oh, it was a disaster at the time, but we laugh about it now. He ruined his rented tuxedo, and my aunt was just mortified. They've been married for forty years now, though, so I suppose a little duck pond incident didn't hurt anything. They just celebrated their anniversary with a cruise to Alaska...

Oh, dear me. I've completely lost the plot again, haven't I? I am so sorry. You were asking about paying attention to movies or lectures. Honestly, I'm not really sure. I don't think I have a problem with that? I mean, I sit through church just fine, and I can watch a movie with my husband without any trouble. I don't really notice my mind wandering off during those things.

Do you ever find yourself avoiding, procrastinating on, or dreading tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort—like writing detailed lesson plans, filling out paperwork, or organizing a big project—because they feel tedious or overwhelming?

Dread lesson plans? Oh, heavens no. I've been writing lesson plans for nearly forty years, so I just sit down and get them done! Though, I will admit, the district just switched to this new online portal for submitting them this year, and it has been quite the learning curve. They brought in this young man to train us on it during an in-service day. He had the most fascinating accent—I think he was from New Zealand? Or maybe Australia. 

My husband Bob and I actually went to Sydney for our twenty-fifth wedding anniversary. Oh, it was a magnificent trip, but the flight was just impossibly long. We flew out of Atlanta, and I made the mistake of wearing these new slip-on shoes that pinched my toes terribly. By the time we landed, my feet were so swollen I couldn't even get them back on! I had to walk through customs in my stocking feet, which was completely mortifying. But the trip was so worth it. We took this boat tour of the harbor and the water was just the most incredible shade of blue, like a sapphire. Bob took so many pictures, he practically filled up three of those little camera memory cards. He loves photography, he actually built a darkroom in our basement back in the nineties...

Oh, my goodness, listen to me. I've taken us all the way to Australia and back! I am so sorry, my brain just hops from one lily pad to the next. You were asking about procrastinating on paperwork or big projects. No, I really don't put that sort of thing off. I just tackle it head-on and get it out of the way!

When you're sitting alone doing something like grading papers or filling out paperwork, do you notice your mind wandering off to unrelated thoughts or getting distracted by things going on around you, even if no one is talking to you?

Distracted when I'm grading papers? Oh, no, not really. I'm pretty good at just sitting down and getting through a stack of essays. I actually like to grade them with a red pen. Well, a red flair pen, specifically. I can't stand ballpoint pens, they always seem to skip on the paper, don't they? I found this wonderful little stationery shop downtown that sells them by the box. The owner is this lovely lady named Margaret. We actually got to talking last time I was in there, and it turns out our daughters were in the same Girl Scout troop back in the nineties! 

Troop 412, it was. I was the cookie mom one year, and let me tell you, having three hundred boxes of Thin Mints stacked in your living room is a true test of willpower. My husband, Bob, used to sneak into the boxes at night. I'd come down in the morning and find empty wrappers stuffed behind the couch cushions! He thought he was being so clever. He's always had a sweet tooth, though. For his birthday last week, I made him a German chocolate cake from scratch. The frosting takes absolutely forever because you have to cook it on the stove until it thickens, and if you turn your back for even a second, it scorches...

Oh, dear. I've done it again, haven't I? I am so sorry, I just get carried away. You were asking if my mind wanders when I'm grading. No, I really don't think it does. I just focus on the task and get it done.

Outside of today's visit, in everyday conversations with friends or family, do you often find that you've lost track of what the other person was saying and need them to repeat themselves, because your own thoughts carried you away?

Lose track of what people are saying? No, I don't think so. I'm a very good listener! I actually love hearing about what my friends are up to. My friend Susan, for instance, she just started taking this pottery class at the community center. She made the most adorable little ceramic birdbath for her garden. She painted it this lovely shade of robin's egg blue, which is my favorite color. I actually painted my guest bathroom that exact color last spring. 

Bob thought it was a bit too bright, but I think it really cheers the space up, especially with those fluffy white towels I found on sale at Macy's. They were having one of those "One Day Sales" that seem to happen every other weekend, you know how they do. I went in just looking for a new spatula and ended up with a whole cart full of things! I found this wonderful little set of espresso cups, even though neither of us drinks espresso. They were just too cute to pass up, with little hand-painted lemons on them. They remind me of the Amalfi Coast. Oh, Bob and I have always wanted to go to Italy, but the flights are just so expensive these days, and with his bad knee...

Oh, for heaven's sake. I'm rambling again! I do apologize. But to answer your question, no, I don't really find myself losing track of what people are saying to me. I'm usually right there in the conversation with them!

Doctor: Have you ever been told that you frequently lose important items—like your keys, wallet, phone, or important documents—because you misplace them or forget where you put them?

Patient: Oh, lose things? Goodness, no. I'm very organized. Everything has its place! I keep my keys on this lovely little brass hook right by the front door. Bob actually installed it for me after we remodeled the entryway. We put down this beautiful hardwood floor, Brazilian cherry, I think it was called. It has such a warm, reddish tone to it. 

Although, let me tell you, keeping it clean with our golden retriever, Buster, was a full-time job! He shed like you wouldn't believe. Every spring, it was just tumbleweeds of golden fur rolling down the hallway. We used to take him to this groomer a few towns over, a sweet girl named Ashley. She always tied a little seasonal bandana around his neck when he was finished. For Halloween one year, she gave him one with little glow-in-the-dark ghosts on it. It was the cutest thing. We actually had a lot of trick-or-treaters that year, probably because Bob went a little overboard and bought full-sized candy bars. He got a whole box of Snickers at Costco. You know, Costco is dangerous like that. You go in for toilet paper and come out with a kayak and a lifetime supply of mayonnaise...

Oh, dear me. Listen to me go on about mayonnaise and dogs! I am so sorry, my train of thought just completely derailed. You were asking if I lose things like my keys or wallet. No, I really don't. I'm very careful about putting things exactly where they belong.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Leaving_Seat
target_item.manifestation: What brought me in is that I keep getting up in meetings or at dinner when everyone else is seated, like I'll suddenly need to refill coffee, check a handout, or walk to the back of the room even though nothing is really urgent.
